# TypeScript guarantees and JavaScript behavior at browser boundaries

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `frontend-typescript-semantics` · **Angular, TypeScript & Frontend Architecture** · Catalog level: foundation

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S06-Q013](#S06-Q013)

<p>What does TypeScript contribute to a frontend codebase, and where do its guarantees end when data arrives at runtime?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Predict frontend behavior by separating static type checks from runtime values, state changes and asynchronous execution.</p>

<ul>
<li>Explain the limit of static typing for data received at runtime.</li>
<li>Predict equality, reassignment and object-mutation outcomes from explicit values.</li>
<li>Explain structural compatibility with a small typed example.</li>
<li>Trace asynchronous results and justify Promise or Observable use for the interaction.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Begin with what TypeScript checks and what still happens in JavaScript. Equality and variable declarations determine how concrete values are compared and changed; structural typing explains which shapes the compiler accepts. Asynchronous results then bring new values into that same state, so ordering and abstraction choices must be explained at the runtime boundary.</p>

### S06-Q013 · Foundation

<p>What does TypeScript contribute to a frontend codebase, and where do its guarantees end when data arrives at runtime?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q013](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q013)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q013](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q013)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain TypeScript's role in a frontend codebase.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the role of static type checking during development and its boundary with executing JavaScript. Use an API payload as a concrete point where that distinction matters.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>State the benefit and limit of TypeScript without confusing types with runtime validation.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the TypeScript version and relevant compiler configuration; verify specific compiler behavior in official documentation. Runtime input is not assumed trustworthy because it has a declared type.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects a type check to a defect it can reveal during development.</li>
<li>Identifies a runtime boundary and explains how its data contract could be checked.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assumes a type annotation or assertion proves that an external payload has the expected shape.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you investigate if typed code receives a field with an unexpected runtime value?</li>
<li>Which compiler configuration matters for the guarantee you just described?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S06-Q011 · Foundation

<p>How do JavaScript&#x27;s == and === comparisons differ, and how would you choose between them when comparing data from a form or API?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q011](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q011)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q011](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q011)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare `==` and `===`.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the comparison rule through values with different types and through objects. The form/API context asks you to apply the rule rather than recite an operator preference.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Predict equality results and justify a comparison at a data boundary.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use ordinary JavaScript values; state the input types. Treat the form/API example as added context, not a source-provided incident.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Predicts results from explicit values and explains the relevant comparison mechanism.</li>
<li>Separates input normalization from comparison and proposes a boundary test.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Repeats an operator rule without accounting for input types or object identity.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you check when a numeric-looking form value fails a comparison?</li>
<li>How would you compare two independently created objects with the same fields?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q012"></a>

### S06-Q012 · Foundation

<p>What changes when a JavaScript variable is declared with let instead of const, including when its value is an object?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q012](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q012)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q012](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q012)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare `let` and `const`.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Distinguish the variable&#x27;s binding, which connects a name to a value, from the contents of that value. Use a small example to explain scope and permitted changes.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Predict reassignment and mutation behavior from a declaration and its scope.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use ordinary JavaScript block-scoped declarations; distinguish primitive and object values. No immutability library is assumed.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains a concrete reassignment versus object-mutation outcome.</li>
<li>Relates the declaration choice to readable intent without claiming it enforces every data invariant.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treats const as proof that an object&#x27;s contents cannot change.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What evidence would show whether an unexpected change was reassignment or mutation?</li>
<li>What additional contract would you need if shared data must remain unchanged?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q014"></a>

### S06-Q014 · Mechanism

<p>What does structural typing mean in TypeScript, and how does it affect whether one object can be used where another type is expected?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q014](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q014)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q014](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q014)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain structural typing at a practical level.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Structural typing concerns compatibility based on shape. Explain it using two small object types and distinguish the compiler&#x27;s decision from the runtime value&#x27;s actual contents.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about type compatibility with an example instead of relying on type names.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State TypeScript version and compiler options; check official documentation for the compatibility rule used in your example. Do not generalize an object-literal check to every assignment context.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Predicts compatibility in a concrete example and explains the relevant shape comparison.</li>
<li>Identifies a boundary of the static guarantee and a case that needs separate validation.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assumes matching type names are required, or that compile-time compatibility proves runtime correctness.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you explain a different result for an object literal and an existing variable?</li>
<li>What must you still check when the object came from an external API?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q015"></a>

### S06-Q015 · Mechanism

<p>How would you explain the order of asynchronous work in a browser, and when are Promises or Observables relevant to that flow?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q015](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q015)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q015](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q015)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain asynchronous browser behavior and Promises/Observables where relevant.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Trace one interaction that starts asynchronous work and later updates the UI. Compare the abstractions only where they change how results, errors or ongoing work are handled.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Predict asynchronous outcomes and justify the abstraction used for the interaction.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify browser context and, if used, Observable-library version and scheduler behavior. Consult official runtime/library documentation before asserting ordering or cancellation guarantees.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains an execution trace rather than equating asynchronous work with parallel threads.</li>
<li>Defines a stale-result or error case and a way to observe the resulting UI state.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treats Promises and Observables as interchangeable without stating how work starts or results arrive.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What happens if an older search request finishes after a newer one?</li>
<li>What exactly does cancellation mean for the abstraction and operation you chose?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A typed product-search screen receives a numeric-looking identifier from a form and JSON objects from an API. Two searches can finish in the opposite order from when they started. Prepare small cases for comparing the identifier, updating an object held by a const binding and accepting a typed shape; then trace which search result should reach the UI. State compiler/runtime/library context and propose an observable test for the stale-result case; do not present an annotation as validation of received JSON.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains the language terms and predicts ordinary comparisons or assignments.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends predictions with mechanisms, separates compiler and runtime guarantees, and handles changed input and asynchronous ordering with a concrete evidence plan.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Only definitions or type annotations are offered, without explicit values, an execution trace or a test of the external-data boundary.</p>
